mainTopic: Laws of מזוזה: how it is written, which side and which doorway it goes on, how it is positioned, and how high it goes
overview: This amud is a series of rulings about how and where to put up a מזוזה. It first finishes שמואל's rule that the מזוזה goes in the outermost טפח of the doorway, not beyond it. Next it rules that a מזוזה written on two sheets is פסולה, and explains away a ברייתא that seems to disagree. It then teaches that the hinge socket (היכר ציר) tells us which side counts as the right side. A story about רב נחמן and the ריש גלותא shows this rule used in practice. רב rules that a מזוזה placed like a bolt is פסולה. The גמרא settles this with the report about רבי's house: lying sideways like a peg is invalid, while standing upright is fine. It also teaches that only the entrance people regularly use needs a מזוזה. Finally, שמואל and רב הונא disagree about how high the מזוזה goes. A ברייתא with רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי seems to leave שמואל without a source, and the answer that he follows רבי יוסי continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why שמואל had to say the מזוזה goes in the טפח near the street
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining what שמואל's ruling adds. Without it, we might think that the farther out the מזוזה is, the better, even outside the doorway. שמואל teaches that it must stay within the doorway's own טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might have thought that the farther the מזוזה is from the inside of the house, the better. So שמואל teaches us that it goes in the טפח right next to the street, and not beyond it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing its answer to the question of what new idea שמואל's ruling teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that the מזוזה goes in the outer part of the doorway. From that, someone might think that going even farther out is better. שמואל's wording sets a limit: the outermost טפח that is still inside the doorway itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a basic unit of measure
The public domain, here meaning the street side of the doorway
Better, preferable
This teaches us; it marks the new idea a statement adds

phrases.english: in the handbreadth adjacent to the public domain,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page, where שמואל ruled that the מזוזה goes in this handbreadth.

phrases.english: [one might think] the further it is, the better,
[so] he teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה דִּמְרַחַק מְעַלֵּי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of שמואל's ruling, which began on the previous page
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the new idea a ruling adds by ruling out a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The farther out the מזוזה is, the better, even beyond the doorway
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזוזה must be in the outermost טפח that is still within the doorway

steps.title: A מזוזה written on two sheets is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if someone wrote a מזוזה on two separate sheets, it is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if someone wrote a מזוזה on two sheets, it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of שמואל about how a מזוזה must be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה has to be written as one unit. Splitting it onto two sheets makes it פסולה, even if all the words are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The parchment with the פרשיות of שמע and והיה אם שמוע, affixed to the doorpost
Sheets or pages of parchment
Invalid, unfit

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one wrote it on two sheets, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the same series of rulings from שמואל about מזוזה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה written on two sheets is פסולה

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow two sheets on one doorpost
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a מזוזה written on two sheets and placed on two doorposts is פסולה. That suggests that if it was placed on one doorpost, it would be כשרה, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We raise an objection from a ברייתא: if someone wrote it on two sheets and put it on two doorposts, it is not valid. That implies that on one doorpost, it would be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא that seems to say two sheets can sometimes be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only calls it פסולה when two separate things happen: two sheets and two doorposts. We infer that two sheets on one doorpost would be כשרה. שמואל said two sheets alone are already פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Doorposts (singular: סַף)
Valid, fit
This implies; it introduces an inference from the wording

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not come from what the ברייתא says outright. It comes from what the ברייתא implies about a case it never mentions: one doorpost.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: If one wrote it on two sheets
and placed it on two doorposts, it is unfit.
This implies that on one doorpost, it is fit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that two sheets are always פסולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא only calls it פסולה when it is on two doorposts. So two sheets on one doorpost would seem to be כשרה.

steps.title: The ברייתא means sheets that could be split onto two doorposts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is not talking about actually placing the sheets on two doorposts. It means the sheets were written so they could be separated onto two doorposts, and that is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא means: if it was written in a way that is fit to be put on two doorposts, it is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא in a new way, so it fits with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'placed it on two doorposts' are reread as 'fit for two doorposts,' meaning the two sheets can be separated from each other. Once the ברייתא no longer talks about the physical placement, there is no inference about one doorpost. שמואל's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for, suitable for
It is saying, meaning: this is what the text really means

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה written on two sheets is פסולה. The ברייתא's 'two doorposts' means sheets that could be split onto two doorposts, not sheets actually hung that way.

phrases.english: It means: fit for two doorposts.
phrases.notes: In other words, the two sheets are written so they could be pulled apart and hung on two different doorposts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is talking about actually placing the sheets on two doorposts, so one doorpost would be fine
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about sheets that could be put on two doorposts, which is פסולה no matter where they are hung

steps.title: Use the hinge to decide which side gets the מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: when deciding which side is the right side for a מזוזה, follow the היכר ציר, the sign given by the door's hinge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for a מזוזה, follow the sign of the hinge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling of שמואל, about how to tell which side of a doorway is the right side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה goes on the right side as you walk in. When it is unclear which direction counts as 'walking in,' the hinge decides it for us.

keyTerms.meaning: Follow, go according to
The sign or indication of the hinge

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
With a mezuza, follow the indication of the hinge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בִּמְזוּזָה, הַלֵּךְ אַחַר הֶיכֵּר צִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in the series of rulings from שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right side of a doorway for a מזוזה is decided by the hinge
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical way to place a מזוזה in doorways that sit between two rooms.

steps.title: What is the hinge indication?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly שמואל means by היכר ציר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'sign of the hinge'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of a term. This sets up רב אדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase היכר ציר is unclear. The גמרא wants to know which physical feature of the door it refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is the indication of the hinge?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what a term in step 5 means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which physical feature 'היכר ציר' refers to

steps.title: רב אדא: it is the hinge socket
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא explains that היכר ציר means the אבקתא, the socket that the hinge turns in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said: it is the socket.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא answers the question by naming the physical feature: the hinge socket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The room on the side where the socket is counts as the room you are entering. The מזוזה goes on the right side as you walk into that room.

keyTerms.meaning: The socket that the door's hinge turns in

phrases.english: Rav Adda said: The socket.
phrases.notes: This is the hole or groove the door's pivot sits in; the room on that side counts as the inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: היכר ציר is the hinge socket (אבקתא)

steps.title: When is this rule needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what kind of case we would need the hinge to tell us which side is the right side.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation שמואל's rule is meant for. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually it is obvious which way is 'in,' because you go from the street into the house. So the גמרא wants to know when the hinge sign is actually needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the rule from steps 5 and 7 applies to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The situation in which the hinge rule is needed

steps.title: A doorway between two rooms, like the men's and women's rooms
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed for a doorway between two rooms of a house, such as between the men's room and the women's room. In that case it is unclear which room counts as 'inside.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, a doorway between two rooms: between the men's room and the women's room.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by describing the case where the hinge rule is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a doorway joins two inner rooms, neither side is clearly the street side. The hinge socket breaks the tie and tells us which room you are entering.

keyTerms.meaning: A doorway or entrance
The men's room or quarters
The women's room or quarters

steps.whatToRemember: In a doorway between two rooms, the room that has the hinge socket counts as the inside. The מזוזה goes on the right side as you enter that room.

phrases.english: For example, an entrance that is between two rooms,
between a men's room and a women's room.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A doorway between two inner rooms, where the direction of entry is unclear

steps.title: רב נחמן tells the Exilarch to hang the doors first
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא built a house and asked רב נחמן to put up מזוזות. רב נחמן told him to hang the doors first, so the hinges would show which side is the right side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא built a house and said to רב נחמן, 'Put up מזוזות for me.' רב נחמן said, 'First hang the doors.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows שמואל's hinge rule being used in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without doors, there are no hinges, and so no sign of which side is the right side. רב נחמן waits for the doors so he can follow the היכר ציר, just as שמואל taught.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the leader of the Jews in בבל
Affix, put up
Doors
First

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that the hinge rule is followed in practice: the doors and hinges should be in place before the מזוזות are affixed.

phrases.english: The Exilarch built a house.
He said to Rav Nachman:
"Affix mezuzot for me."
Rav Nachman said: "Hang the doors first."
phrases.notes: He needs the doors up so the hinges show which side counts as the right side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the hinge rule from steps 5 through 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doors and hinges should be hung before the מזוזות are affixed, so that the היכר ציר can be followed

steps.title: A מזוזה placed like a bolt is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a מזוזה placed like a bolt is פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: if someone placed the מזוזה like a bolt, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב. If a מזוזה is put on the doorpost like a bolt, it does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bolt lies sideways and slides into a hole. So רב is saying that a מזוזה placed in that kind of position is not a valid way to fulfill the מצוה. This rule about the shape of the placement sets up the challenge that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A bolt or bar, the kind that slides sideways into a hole to lock a door
He made it / placed it

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
If he made it like a kind of bolt,
phrases.notes: Picture the מזוזה lying sideways or pushed into a hole in the doorpost, the way a door bolt sits.

phrases.english: it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from where the מזוזה goes (the right side) to how it is positioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מזוזה placed like a bolt is פסולה.

steps.title: But the mezuzot in רבי's house were like bolts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a report about רבי's house. All the מזוזות there were made like a bolt, and רבי's own entrance to the בית מדרש had no מזוזה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said that all the מזוזות in רבי's house were made like a bolt. He also said that the doorway רבי used to enter the בית מדרש had no מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's rule. רבי, the great leader, had bolt-style מזוזות in his own house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי's house used bolt-style מזוזות, then that style must be valid, which goes against רב. The report also includes a second surprising fact: רבי's doorway into the בית מדרש had no מזוזה. The גמרא will deal with that second fact separately in steps 14-15.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
The house of רבי יהודה הנשיא
The study hall
When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר:
phrases.english: But when Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:
All the mezuzot of Rabbi's house
were made like a kind of bolt,
and that doorway through which Rabbi entered
into the study hall
did not have a mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a bolt-style מזוזה is פסולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's house used bolt-style מזוזות, so that style must be valid. The report's second fact, that רבי's study-hall doorway had no מזוזה, is taken up separately in steps 14-15.

steps.title: Lying sideways like a peg versus standing upright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the invalid case is a מזוזה placed sideways like a peg. רבי's מזוזות stood upright like an ankle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a difficulty. This case, the invalid one, is where it is made like a peg. That case, the valid one, is where it is made like an ankle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. There are two different kinds of 'bolt-style' placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's פסול case is a מזוזה lying sideways and pushed in like a peg. רבי's מזוזות were set in the doorpost but standing up straight, like an ankle bone. Standing upright is valid, so רב and the report about רבי do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty. Used to open an answer that splits two cases
A peg; here, a מזוזה lying sideways, pushed into the post
An ankle; here, a מזוזה standing upright

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where it is made like a peg,
phrases.notes: This is רב's invalid case: the מזוזה lies sideways, pushed into the post.

phrases.english: that is where it is made like an ankle.
phrases.notes: This is the valid case, the kind רבי had: the מזוזה stands up straight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): two different kinds of placement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any bolt-like placement is the same, so רבי's house contradicts רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sideways like a peg is פסול. Upright like an ankle is כשר, and that is what רבי had.

steps.title: But רב הונא's study-hall entrance had a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי's entrance to the בית מדרש had no מזוזה. The entrance רב הונא used to enter the בית מדרש did have one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But the doorway through which רב הונא used to enter the בית מדרש did have a מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second part of רב יצחק בר יוסף's report. It asks why רבי's study-hall doorway would have no מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's doorway into the בית מדרש had a מזוזה. That suggests a study-hall entrance needs one. So how could רבי's entrance have been without a מזוזה?

keyTerms.meaning: Enters

phrases.english: Is that so?
But that doorway

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה עָיֵיל בַּהּ רַב הוּנָא לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא,
phrases.english: through which Rav Huna would enter the study hall,
did have a mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא הָהוּא פִּיתְחָא דַּהֲוָה עָיֵיל בַּהּ רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second half of step 12 (רבי's entrance with no מזוזה) and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי's entrance to the בית מדרש had no מזוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's study-hall entrance had a מזוזה, so study-hall entrances should need one.

steps.title: Follow the entrance people regularly use
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's entrance was the regular one everyone used. For מזוזה, we follow the regular entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: That doorway was the regular one, as רב יהודה said in the name of רב: regarding מזוזה, follow the regular one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between the two doorways. רב הונא's doorway was the main entrance that everyone used, so it needed a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's doorway was a side door used only by him, so it was not the 'regular' entrance and did not need a מזוזה. The answer is backed by a general rule from רב: for מזוזה, we go by the entrance people usually use.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular; the entrance people usually use
Go by the regular entrance

steps.whatToRemember: A מזוזה must stand upright, not lie sideways like a peg. When there are several doorways, the one people regularly use is the one that needs a מזוזה.

phrases.english: That one was the regular one,
phrases.notes: רב הונא's doorway was the main one everyone used, while רבי's was a side door just for him.

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
With a mezuzah, follow the regular one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא רְגִיל הֲוָה, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a regular entrance versus a private side entrance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every study-hall entrance needs a מזוזה, so רבי's entrance should have had one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the regularly used entrance needs one. רבי's private side door did not.

steps.title: שמואל: place it at the start of the upper third
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the מצוה is to put the מזוזה at the beginning of the upper third of the doorpost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב מתנא, who said in the name of שמואל: it is a מצוה to place it at the beginning of the upper third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: how high on the doorpost the מזוזה should go. שמואל gives a specific spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture the doorpost divided into three equal parts. שמואל says the best place is where the top third begins. He calls it a מצוה, meaning this is the proper way to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a מצוה (the proper way) to place it
The upper third (of the doorpost)
At the beginning of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Matna said that Shmuel said:
It is a מצוה to place it
at the beginning of the upper third,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the height of the מזוזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזוזה should ideally go at the start of the upper third of the doorpost.

steps.title: רב הונא: anywhere between a handbreadth from top and bottom
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the whole doorpost is כשר for a מזוזה, as long as it is a טפח above the floor and a טפח below the top beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: one raises it a טפח from the ground and keeps it a טפח away from the beam, and the whole doorway is כשר for the מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a different, wider view. Almost the whole height of the doorpost works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל points to one ideal spot. רב הונא only rules out the bottom טפח and the top טפח. Anywhere in between is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The beam across the top of the doorway (the lintel)
Valid; fit for the מצוה

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
One raises it a handbreadth from the ground,
and keeps it a handbreadth away from the beam,
and the entire doorway is fit for the mezuzah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא אָמַר: מַגְבִּיהַּ מִן הַקַּרְקַע טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמואל's view in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anywhere on the doorpost is כשר except the bottom טפח and the top טפח.

steps.title: A baraita: רבי יהודה allows anywhere, רבי יוסי requires the top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says what רב הונא said. רבי יוסי learns from the פסוקים that the מזוזה must be high up, the way תפילין are bound high on the arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: one raises it a טפח from the ground and keeps it a טפח from the beam, and the whole doorway is כשר for the מזוזה. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: the Torah says 'and you shall bind them' and 'and you shall write them.' Just as binding is done high up, so too writing is done high up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge the views it just brought. It is setting up a problem that it will spell out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's words match רב הונא exactly. רבי יוסי links the פסוק about תפילין ('and you shall bind them') to the next פסוק about מזוזה ('and you shall write them'). Since תפילין go on the upper part of the arm, the מזוזה must go on the upper part of the doorway. Neither opinion sounds exactly like שמואל's 'beginning of the upper third,' so the coming challenge seems aimed at שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall bind them,' the פסוק about תפילין
'And you shall write them,' the פסוק about מזוזה
Binding (of the תפילין)
Writing; here it means putting up the מזוזה
High up; on the upper part

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not a challenge to רב הונא. רבי יהודה says the same thing he does. The problem is aimed at שמואל, whose 'start of the upper third' does not exactly match either opinion.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One raises it a handbreadth from the ground,
and keeps it a handbreadth away from the beam,
and the entire doorway is fit for the mezuzah;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
"And you shall bind them," "and you shall write them,"
phrases.notes: דברים 6:8 and 6:9, two פסוקים right next to each other.

phrases.english: just as binding is high up,
phrases.notes: He means the תפילין are tied on the upper part of the arm.

phrases.english: so too writing is high up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the two views on height from steps 16-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Apparently שמואל's 'beginning of the upper third'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה allows the whole doorpost and רבי יוסי requires the upper part. שמואל's specific spot does not clearly match either one. The גמרא spells this out in the next lines.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion about which תנא שמואל agrees with. It also shows the source for putting the מזוזה high up: the link between תפילין and מזוזה.

steps.title: שמואל's ruling seems to match neither תנא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא fits רבי יהודה, but שמואל seems to fit neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רב הונא: he holds like רבי יהודה. But שמואל, whose opinion is he following? He is not following רבי יהודה, and he is not following רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the challenge from the ברייתא in step 18. It shows that שמואל's ruling has no clear source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says the whole doorpost is כשר, which is exactly רב הונא's view. רבי יוסי says the מזוזה must be high up, like תפילין. שמואל says 'the beginning of the upper third.' That is not 'anywhere,' and it does not seem to be 'at the top' either, so his view looks unsupported.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side, but there is a problem with the other)
Like whom? (which תנא does this follow?)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not that שמואל is wrong. The point is that an אמורא's ruling should match some תנא, and here it seems to match none.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Huna,
he states his ruling in line with Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רב הונא said the whole doorpost is fine. That is the same as רבי יהודה in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: but Shmuel, who said his ruling: in line with whom?
phrases.notes: שמואל said the מזוזה goes at the beginning of the upper third (step 16).

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי!
phrases.english: Not in line with Rabbi Yehuda, and not in line with Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הוּנָא הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge that the ברייתא in step 18 raises against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the מזוזה goes at the beginning of the upper third (step 16)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two תנאים give two options: anywhere (רבי יהודה) or high up (רבי יוסי). שמואל's 'beginning of the upper third' seems to fit neither, so it has no source among the תנאים.

steps.title: שמואל actually follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן answers that שמואל really does follow רבי יוסי. His explanation continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב נתן said: Really, שמואל follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer begins. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן claims שמואל does follow רבי יוסי. This line sets up the explanation of how that can work, which comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לעולם means 'in truth, I stand by this,' even though it looked impossible a moment ago. So the answer must show that רבי יוסי's 'high up' can match 'the beginning of the upper third.' That reading is about to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (holding on to a position despite the challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This רב הונא בריה דרב נתן is a different person from the רב הונא whose ruling was discussed in steps 17 and 19.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, said:
Actually, Shmuel's ruling is in line with Rabbi Yosei,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 19's challenge by placing שמואל with רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a תנא's view so it matches the אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי's 'high up' could not match 'the beginning of the upper third.'
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי יוסי. The explanation of how continues on the next amud.
